natural_body: 40% SMB discount: +31% signups, +18% rev, -12% ret; judge at renewal

first.rationale: Given capacity for only one experiment, I prioritize addressing the two internally-controllable metrics that are currently declining (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) rather than reacting to competitor pricing pressure. Memory_31 and memory_86 both support onboarding simplification as a durable, low-risk lever for activation and completion. Promotional_pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor SMB price pressure, but the archived record explicitly flags a -12% retention effect pending renewal judgment, which conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; matching competitor discounting could erode margin and retention further without verified long-term upside. I verify memory_73 to confirm the retention risk is real and not stale, and memory_31 to confirm the onboarding lift is durable and applicable to current SMB conditions before committing scarce experiment capacity. I'm running this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout because activation/onboarding metrics have shifted since these memories were consolidated (days 12 and 52), and competitive dynamics may have changed user behavior in ways not captured in the original records.
